title: A Practical Plan for the Success Sequence
author: Institute for Family Studies
source: Institute for Family Studies Digest, April 24, 2026
summary: IFS research identifies the 'success sequence'—finish education, secure stable employment, marry, and then have children—as a powerful predictor of economic stability and family wellbeing. Yet modern culture discourages this sequence, instead promoting individual achievement at the expense of family formation. Young adults who follow the success sequence report higher economic security and relationship stability. The sequence works because each step provides structure and motivation for the next. Yet cultural messaging consistently encourages women to establish their careers before marriage and parenthood, often resulting in delayed or foregone family formation. The research suggests that young adults should understand the genuine goods of following this sequence.
points: The success sequence—education, employment, marriage, children—predicts economic and relational stability.
Modern culture discourages this sequence in favor of indefinite career prioritization.
Young people who follow the sequence report higher economic security and family satisfaction.
Understanding the sequence helps young adults make intentional choices about timing and priorities.
quotes: The success sequence—education, employment, marriage, children—is a practical path to stability.
Those who follow the sequence report higher economic security and relationship satisfaction.
The key insight is that each step provides structure for the next.” Archived from Institute for Family Studies Digest on May 2, 2026 by Tim.
